label: Person
name: Pha Mueang
summary:
Pha Mueang or Pho Khun Pha Mueang was a Thai nobleman and general who played a pivotal role in the founding of the Sukhothai Kingdom.

Born into the royal family, his ascension to power marked the beginning of Sukhothai's rise as a major force in Southeast Asian politics.

In 1257, Pha Mueang led the forces of the Sukhothai Empire against the Khmer Empire, securing a crucial victory at the Battle of Wiang Chan.

The victory cemented Sukhothai's dominance over its neighbors and paved the way for the establishment of the city as an imperial capital.

Pha Mueang's military campaigns also helped to spread Theravada Buddhism throughout the region, further solidifying his legacy as a unifying figure in Thai history.

He died in 1300, leaving behind a lasting impact on the political and cultural landscape of Sukhothai and beyond.
